en: The Sūtra of the Noble Adornment Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha,
Volume One. Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Rank of Chao San Da Fu, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, the Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was staying at the city of Kapilavastu in the Aśoka Grove.
Together with a great assembly of bhikṣus, such as Ānanda,
and the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, they gathered in one place. At that time,
there were also hosts of devas, hosts of nāgas, and hosts of yakṣas.
The hosts of rākṣasas, the hosts of asuras,
the hosts of garuḍas, the hosts of gandharvas,
the hosts of kiṃnaras, and the hosts of piśācas.
The hosts of Pīṭhas, the hosts of Kumbhāṇḍas,
the hosts of Bhūtanās, the hosts of Graspers,
and the twenty-eight great Yakṣa army commanders.
The hosts of the four great yakṣa generals,
all the hosts of stellar deities,
and even the hosts of various sages practicing austerities on the Snowy Mountains.
Thus, all these hosts gathered together.
Furthermore, there were all the hosts of rākṣasas from other directions, namely:
the gaṇis, bhūtas, nāgas, kiṃnaras, kumbhāṇḍas, sumanas, mahāhārīs, and mātṛs.
Such multitudes as these also gathered there.
Furthermore, there were four great rākṣasīs from the four directions,
namely, the rākṣasī Hari in the east.
In the south is the rākṣasa Yūnara;
in the west is the rākṣasa Kiśarī;
in the north is the rākṣasa Maṇitandata.
These four rākṣasas are by nature extremely violent and malevolent;
each has sixty attendants.
These rākṣasas have also come to this assembly.
At that time, while the youth Rāhula was lying down at night in King Śuddhodana’s palace, he was harassed by an evil rākṣasa;
repeatedly terrified, he could find no peace.
At that time, Rāhula’s mother Yaśodharā and her entire retinue all learned that the World-Honored One and the assembly of noble ones were in the Aśoka Grove,
not far from the palace city.
In the latter part of the night, he had Rāhula,
accompanied by a group of youths and various attendants leading and following him, go to where the Buddha was.
Then the youth Rāhula, having arrived at the assembly of the Buddha,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and stood alone before the Buddha weeping.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Ānanda, did you see the youth Rāhula come to me and weep?
Ānanda replied, "Indeed, I saw him."
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
"When the youth Rāhula is lying down at night,
he is [beset] by evil rākṣasas and various kinds of spirits."
They come to harass and disturb him so that he cannot find peace and security;
therefore, they have come to me to seek my protection.
Ānanda, it is not only today that the youth Rāhula has done so.
They will disturb one another and find no peace.
After my parinirvāṇa, during the final age,
the power of merit of all sentient beings will be weak and inferior.
Unwholesome karma increases and becomes intense;
consequently, various evil rākṣasas,
spirits, and other such beings roam throughout the world.
They constantly bring harm to sentient beings,
afflicting them in various ways so that they find no peace.
Observing this matter, I feel deep compassion for them.
Ānanda, I now, for the sake of protecting the youth Rāhula and out of compassion for future sentient beings,
shall proclaim the Mahāvyūha Dhāraṇī.
"You should listen attentively.
At that time, Ānanda and the great assembly were all silent,
each wishing for the Buddha to proclaim his teaching.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this Great Adornment Dhāraṇī, saying:

*Tadyathā | gani | garāgaṇapate | gumigara | gumabhatiṣparika | garipati | sarapati | dhanapati | surapati | ale | anale | panapati | manapati | abhāti | va* (The Sanskrit text provided contains several orthographic variations and potential scribal errors; the above transcription reflects the phonetic rendering as closely as possible based on the input.)

Hūṃ pātrī hūṃ hrīḥ grahū udrīḥ prahrīḥ oṃ jñaptī pātra-pāṭa ṭhaṭha vighna-hara oṃ rāve maṇi-sarī hūṃ mahā-hrīḥ hu hu samanta-sasari asamanta-sari pare kha-sari ā-vandita mahā-vandite gani-mikhale hūṃ svāhā. Ānanda, this is the Great Adornment Dhāraṇī.
This was indeed proclaimed by all the Buddhas of the past.
Now, for the sake of protecting the youth Rāhula and likewise to benefit the sentient beings of the final age, I [speak it].
Now I shall proclaim it once more:
Ānanda, if there are sentient beings who are tormented by various rākṣasas and malevolent spirits, causing them manifold disturbances;
One should write this Adornment Dhāraṇī upon paper or silk,
fashion it into a *pratisara* amulet, and wear it upon one's body or arm;
this shall cause all evil rākṣasas [to be subdued].
Even all those in the world who subsist on fat and blood,
as well as the classes of malevolent spirits and ghosts, dare not approach;
they all flee, avoiding it from afar for ten yojanas in the four cardinal and four intermediate directions.
I shall cause all sentient beings to attain peace and happiness.
Ānanda, if there are sentient beings who constantly read and recite this Great Adornment Dhāraṇī, [they shall likewise attain such blessings].
All weapons, staves, poisons, and drugs shall be unable to cause harm;
even the binding of wicked spells, incantations, and nooses—
whether by humans or non-humans— and all such evil matters shall be completely liberated.
Within a range of ten yojanas,
all sentient beings shall receive protection,
and all calamities and misfortunes shall be entirely extinguished.
Ānanda, if there are sentient beings who wish to uphold and recite this Great Adornment Dhāraṇī to protect themselves and to bring benefit to all sentient beings, [they should do so].
First, one should select a pure and superior location and establish markers in advance; then,
one should personally observe the fast and precepts and bathe with scented water.
One should cause the body and mind to be pure both internally and externally.
Using thread, one should demarcate the boundary and smear the ground with fragrant mud to construct a maṇḍala.
Within the maṇḍala, one should prepare various kinds of famous flowers.
Having made various offerings of unguents,
incense, and lamps, sit upright facing north and, with right mindfulness, visualize that the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
has descended into the maṇḍala.
Thereafter, one should present various offerings,
take refuge, and offer praise;
with a firm mind, one should exert oneself with vigor and never retreat.
In order to benefit and protect all sentient beings,
and to seek the accomplishment of present activities,
one should first recite the *Dhāraṇī for the Adornment of the Boundaries*.
With alert awareness, he summons Brahmā, Śakra, and all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and other spirits to assemble;
they shall cause all those who afflict and harm sentient beings in the world to be subdued.
When all the evil yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas,
and others have heard this dhāraṇī,
they will be struck with terror and disperse; free from all obstacles and difficulties, their aspirations shall be fulfilled.
Then he spoke the *dhāraṇī* for binding the boundary (*sīmābandha*), saying:
*tadyathā | nile nile vimale tamale guñje guñje śrīdri tri tri sāni raḥ svāhā*. Ānanda, if one has recited this *dhāraṇī* for the adornment of the boundary, [the boundary is established].
Thereafter, one should recite that Noble Mahāvyūha Dhāraṇī;
then all undertakings will be accomplished without exception.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Maitreya rose from his seat.
Standing before the Buddha, he addressed him, saying: "World-Honored One,
I too desire to protect the youth Rāhula so that he may attain peace and security,
and I likewise desire to benefit all sentient beings of the future."
All those who are afflicted by various torments,
as well as all evil persons with swords, staves, poisons, and drugs,
or who are bound by malevolent spells, fetters, and nooses.
May all such matters as these lead to complete liberation;
may they dwell in peace and happiness throughout day and night.
Furthermore, I shall proclaim the Adornment Dhāraṇī.
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will grant me permission to proclaim this.
The Buddha said, "You may do as you wish."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Maitreya spoke this Adornment Dhāraṇī, saying:

*Tadyathā | āvanati pavanati avinānujūru jūru jaridhani dhanani adhādhani samantadhani nirmuni nirmi muñci śānti svastiṣṭaya namo mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca rakṣa kuru svāhā.* Then, the Great Brahmā Deva-king, Lord of the Sahā World...
He then addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I also wish to protect the youth Rāhula,
as well as to protect all sentient beings of the future."
"I shall now explain the *Svālaṃkāra-vidyā*.
I pray that the Tathāgata will grant me permission to proclaim it.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent! You may speak according to your own intention."
Then the Great Brahmā King immediately spoke this mantra of adornment:

*traṃ vīra-tantraṃ hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ | anu-rūṃ nu-rūṃ | śrī-kṣetraṃ kṣetraṃ hūṃ | nu-du-rūṃ nū-rūṃ ra-ya-ti | ā-ja ā-ja vi-muca śāntiṃ svā-sty-ayaṃ ya-nāṃ kuru mama sarva-sattvānāṃ ca svāhā.* At that time, the World-Honored One...
He knew that the hosts of devas, nāgas, yakṣas,
and all the various spirits each desired to protect the youth Rāhula and future sentient beings.
All of them wished to proclaim their own mantras.
The Buddha said, "O you hosts of devas, nāgas, and various spirits,
you who wish to proclaim your own mantras for the purpose of protecting all sentient beings."
"Speak each according to your own intention.
At that time, the deity Kālacakra (Good Time) spoke his own vidyā-mantra before the Buddha:

*Trividha-durllabha-saṃciti saṃciti rudrākaraṇi ghanir-nuru-nuri-muñje-śakri-rājye śānti-puṣṭi svastyayanaṃ kārūṇya-marmollikha-kuru svāhā.* The Holy *Ārya-vyūha-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, Volume One. The Holy *Ārya-vyūha-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, Volume Two.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao-san Dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
Translated by the Dharma-transmitting Master, the Subject Shi Hu, by imperial decree.
At that time, Śakra Devānām Indra spoke this mantra of his own adornment:
Trayambakaṃ yajāmahe sugandhiṃ puṣṭivardhanam | Urvārukamiva bandhanān mṛtyormukṣīya mā'mṛtāt svāhā || At that time, the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa...
The mantra for self-adornment is proclaimed as follows:
*tryadhvatathatānugatajñānakṣitigarbha āveśaya māṃ sarvasattvānāṃ ca jñānavatīm abhimukhīkuru svāhā*. At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra...
The mantra for self-adornment is proclaimed as follows:

*Oṃ traya-buddhadhāri dhāri dhāraṇi dhāri ajayite pramukhe śānti-puṣṭi-svastya-yanānāṃ mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca rakṣaṇa-kāruṇika-jyotirmat-pradīpa-vandye svāhā.* At that time, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka...
The mantra for his own adornment is proclaimed as follows:

*trayadhvatīrṇa dhanu nāriṃ bhaṃtariṃ karaṃte karaṃbante karurupe karidhare kaṅka-patari ruru-mikṣa mikṣa mi ākṣami pākṣa śāntiṃ svasti sarvathānām mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca rakṣa kuru yavakṣemaṃ parivandhaya vaṭu svāhā*. At that time, the Great Heavenly King Virūpākṣa...
The mantra for self-adornment is proclaimed as follows:
*tryadhvatathāgatajvala jvala jaṭāmakuṭe ṭiri ṭiri kari kari samantakīri kīri śānte svastaye sarvabhūtānāṃ cāya vācamaṇḍenakāruṇi svāhā*. At that time, the Devaputra Candracchattra...
The mantra for self-adornment is proclaimed as follows:

*Oṃ vande vimale prasavāśritāśme sahāśme pratitiṣṭha svasti svasti siddhyāyaṃ kuru mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca vyāpamaṃ daṅkārūṇi svāhā*. At that time, the entire assembly of devas spoke with one voice in unison.
The mantra for the Adornment of Light (*Vairocanavyūha*) is proclaimed as follows:

*trayadhvatathāgatānāṃ kulukulu sulusulu pulupulu śāntiṃ kuru svasti sarvabhūtānāṃ jīvavarma bandhaya kuru mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca rakṣa māṃ durgatiṃ ca svāhā*. At that time, all the celestial bodies (*nakṣatradevatās*) spoke with one voice in unison.
The mantra for the Adornment of Light is spoken as follows:

*tryadhvatathāgate dharmate āle nāle ākāśavimalaśānte svastyayanaṃ kuru me mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca jayavajramantraṃ kuru me svāhā*. At that time, all the hosts of nāgas, with one voice and in unison, [spoke].
The mantra for the Adornment of Light is proclaimed as follows:

*traya-viṣaya-dhanava-le-male-ajale-maṭi-aśumati-pūjya-śānti-svastya-yānāṃ kuru mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca jayavācamaṇḍenakāruṇi svāhā*. At that time, the assembly of the twenty-eight great yakṣa army commanders...
With one voice and in unison, they spoke this mantra of adornment:
*Trayadhvatathāgatapate pata ruru dāra dāra śāntiṃ svasti ca yaccha sarvasattvānāṃ jayavajramantraṃ kuru me svāhā*. At that time, the hosts of bhūtas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, and so forth...
With one voice and in unison, they spoke this mantra of adornment:
*Oṃ tryambaka-tuṣṭi-svāhā, tvaṃ tiṣṭha saṃstutya svastyayanaṃ mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca jayavajramandakāruṇi svāhā*. At that time, the assembly of Bhūtāṇḍa and Kaṭabhūtāṇḍa...
With one voice and in unison, they spoke this mantra of adornment:
*Oṃ traya-bhava-nirmāṇa-kārite tathāgata-sarva-samaya-mudre svasti śānti-puṣṭi-svastyayanaṃ kuru me mama sarva-sattva-śokāpaha-vyādhi-praśamana-kāre svāhā*. At that time, all the mātṛkās...
With one voice and in unison, they spoke this mantra of adornment and illumination:
*trayabhatika leme līdri dṛdramari śāntiṃ svasti ca yānāṃ karomi mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca vyādhimardanakaromi svāhā*. At that time, the four rākṣasīs from the four directions...
With one voice and in unison, they spoke this mantra of adornment:
*tryambaka-ānīpānīkhañje khañjavaje khukhure pe parihare śānti svasti ca yānāṃ kāruṇika mama sarvasattvānāṃ ca jayavāmamaṃtraṃ kāruṇika svāhā*. At that time, the rākṣasī Narmadā...
The Ornament of Illumination (Abhisamayālaṃkāra) states:

*Trinayatrāṇanāri nāri ha ha ha ha hi hi hi hi hu hu hu hu śi ci ci ci ji ci ji vi mukhe makha ja kha khiccha mi tsi aṇṭha aṇṭha ṭara ṭara krama ja ku ru ku ru nu nu nu nu ru nu ru taru che me li mi me li ana ko ko khami nu nu nu ti ti mi ti ni ti li mi tsi ji ti mi tsi li tsi pi tsi pi tra pi tra pi ni nu he ni mu he ni ra he va he na cha pi ye.* At that time, Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, [spoke].
They addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One, we— the hosts of devas,
nāgas, yakṣas, and even the nirmāṇaratis—
all these hosts now stand before the World-Honored One at this very moment."
Each spoke of their own illumination, desiring to protect the youth Rāhula so that no evil spirits or ghostly beings might approach,
harass, or disturb him.
We obtain security by day and security by night;
at all times, we attain abiding in happiness.
World-Honored One, what we have spoken is self-evident.
It is not only that he protects the youth Rāhula;
he also acts as a protector for all sentient beings of the future.
World-Honored One, if there are sentient beings...
Upon hearing these mantras of ours,
you must mindfully recollect and uphold them with a sincere heart.
You shall cause all those various types of beings who act to our disadvantage— whether within one yojana, two yojanas, three or four yojanas, or even up to ten yojanas— to be [subdued].
They dare not approach, but are terrified and disperse, fleeing far away.
Thus, within ten *yojanas*,
all evils are extinguished and pestilence does not prevail.
They will be entirely free from weapons and poisons,
and they shall not be obstructed by any devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, or mahoragas.
Furthermore, they shall not be obstructed by any bhūtas or non-human beings.
World-Honored One, should any among such multitudes as these act in opposition or fail to comply, [they shall likewise be hindered].
That assembly would not tolerate him and would expel him from the clan.
At that time, the World-Honored One said to Ānanda:
"This Great Brahmā Deva King stands before me."
"I have personally realized and known these words of truth.
Ānanda, this Great Adornment Dhāraṇī which I have proclaimed possesses great power and is able to subdue all evils."
I have already previously explained that which brings benefit.
Ānanda, if there should be another person who,
by means of all those heterodox spells and incantations of humans and non-humans alike, [attempts to harm them].
They seek to seize, bind, and afflict sentient beings in various ways—
whether on the earth, in the air,
at the foot of mountains, on mountain peaks, or in any place whatsoever.
"By the majestic power of my Noble Adornment Dhāraṇī,
they shall all be utterly destroyed and will be unable to cause harm to any sentient beings.
The Buddha then spoke again to Ānanda:
The Buddha is real, the Dharma is real, and the Sangha is real;
the devas are real and the ṛṣis are real.
These five are such that they cannot be contravened.
Ānanda, you must skillfully receive and uphold what I have taught,
so that it may circulate in the world in the future and bring great benefit to all sentient beings.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra,
the youth Rāhula heard the World-Honored One’s exposition of the Great Adornment Dhāraṇī and was protected by the reception of all vidyās.
Not departing from this assembly, they attained peace and happiness;
their minds were joyful and they leaped for joy.
They prostrated with their heads upon the ground, paying homage at the feet of the Tathāgata.
Together with his attendants, he returned to the royal palace;
so too did Maitreya Bodhisattva,
Ānanda, and all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, humans, and non-humans.
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they received it with joy and faith, prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
*The Sūtra on the Holy Adornment Dhāraṇī*, Scroll II.
